name: crc32fast (SIMD CRC-32/IEEE)
baseline: crc crate 1.8.1 in the README table; today's crc 3.x defaults to a 256-entry table
verdict_reason: The README's 35x lead (7314 MB/s vs 207 MB/s) is against crc 1.8.1. crc 3.4 reports 0.516 GiB/s for its default bytewise CRC-32 and 3.30 GiB/s with Slice16 on a Ryzen 7 3800X, so against the current crate the gap is roughly 13x for the default and 2x for Slice16, comparing numbers from different machines. The PCLMULQDQ path is still the fastest of the three.
tier_reason: First-party table from crc32fast 1.0.0 with no CPU, OS, rustc or input size stated.
claimed_speedup: 7314 MB/s (pclmulqdq) and 1499 MB/s (baseline table path) vs 207 MB/s for crc 1.8.1 (35x and 7x, derived from page data). Against crc 3.x measured on another machine: 0.516 GiB/s default bytewise, 3.30 GiB/s Slice16 (about 13x and 2x, derived from page data).
workload: CRC-32 (IEEE) over one buffer; size not stated (the ns/iter and MB/s columns imply about 1 KB, derived from page data).
platforms: x86/x86_64 (SSE + PCLMULQDQ; VPCLMULQDQ with AVX2/AVX-512 on Rust 1.89+), aarch64 CRC32 instructions, table fallback elsewhere; no_std without SIMD
one_liner: CRC-32/IEEE with runtime-selected PCLMULQDQ or ARMv8 CRC instructions; 7.3 GB/s in its own table, far ahead of table-driven CRC.
how_it_is_fast: On x86 it folds the input with carry-less multiplication (PCLMULQDQ, or VPCLMULQDQ on 256- and 512-bit registers), processing many bytes per instruction instead of a table lookup per byte. On aarch64 it uses the hardware crc32 instructions with 3-way interleaving to hide latency. Hasher::new picks the implementation at runtime; the fallback still processes 16 bytes per iteration.
use_it_when: zip, gzip, PNG and other formats that need CRC-32/IEEE
Checksumming large buffers on x86_64 or aarch64
skip_it_when: You need CRC-32C (Castagnoli) or another polynomial: crc32fast computes CRC-32/IEEE only
no_std builds, where runtime detection and so the SIMD paths are unavailable
caveats: The table is from crc32fast 1.0.0; the newer AVX2/AVX-512 VPCLMULQDQ paths have no published numbers
The baseline crc 1.8.1 is long superseded
No CPU stated; the crc 3.x numbers come from a different machine
tradeoffs: unsafe SIMD intrinsics, fuzzed and run under AddressSanitizer in CI per the README
